<div class="page-intro page-intro-compact">
<p class="eyebrow">About</p>
<h1>Background and research</h1>
<p class="page-dek">From economics in Ghana to doctoral research in Bayesian statistics, my work has developed across methods and applications.</p>
</div>

<div class="about-layout">
<div class="essay">
<p>I am completing a PhD in Statistics at <a href="https://www.qmul.ac.uk/">Queen Mary University of London (QMUL)</a>, affiliated with the <a href="https://www.kew.org/">Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew</a>. My doctoral research, supervised by <a href="https://www.qmul.ac.uk/maths/profiles/liveranis.html">Professor Silvia Liverani</a>, <a href="https://www.qmul.ac.uk/sbbs/staff/andrewleitch.html">Professor Andrew Leitch</a>, and <a href="https://www.kew.org/science/our-science/people/ilia-j-leitch">Dr Ilia J. Leitch</a>, focuses on Bayesian statistics with applications in ecology, particularly Bayesian spatial modelling for biodiversity.</p>
<h2>Academic journey</h2>
<p>My academic journey began in Ghana, where I studied economics at the <a href="https://uds.edu.gh/">University for Development Studies (UDS)</a> in Tamale. Afterward, I served as a teaching and administrative assistant for one year in the Department of Economics. Working closely with <a href="https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=s51i5HAAAAAJ&hl=en">Professor Haruna Issahaku</a>, <a href="https://portal.pep-net.org/public/researcher/14360">Professor Paul Kwame Nkegbe</a>, and <a href="https://ubids.edu.gh/dcobi/director-profile">Professor Stanley Kojo Dary</a> was an inspiring experience that led to my first steps into academic research and writing.</p>
<p>I later pursued postgraduate study in France at the <a href="https://www.ube.fr/en/home/">University of Burgundy Europe (UBE)</a> in Dijon. During this time, I completed a two-month internship at <a href="https://econresuam.wordpress.com/interns/">ECONRES</a> at the <a href="https://www.uam.es/uam/inicio">Autonomous University of Madrid (AUM)</a> in Madrid, Spain. There, I worked with <a href="https://corochasco.wordpress.com/">Professor Coro Chasco</a> and <a href="https://sites.google.com/site/legallopage/home">Professor Julie Le Gallo</a> on structural equation modelling, an experience that further deepened my interest in research at the intersection of economics and statistics.</p>
<h2>Methods and applications</h2>
<p>Across my research interests and experience, Bayesian inference, statistical modelling, and uncertainty quantification provide a common thread. I am interested in econometrics, environmental modelling, and health data modelling alongside ecological applications, where these methods help make incomplete, biased, or noisy data more interpretable.</p>
